troubleshooting.title: The Git Client Reports a Filesystem Name Collision
troubleshooting.shortdesc: Two tracked files whose names differ only in letter case or accent map to the same file on your file system, so the Git Client flags them and holds off risky operations.

condition.title: Problem
condition.p:
A Filesystem name collision warning appears in the view, and one or more files in the
area are marked with a Path Collision icon. You cannot stage or discard those files, and stashing — along with the pull and pre-push operations that stash internally — is refused.

cause.title: Cause
cause.p: Two files tracked in the repository have names that differ only in letter case or Unicode form — for example, an accented and an unaccented spelling of the same name. On a case-insensitive or Unicode-folding file system (such as macOS APFS or Windows), both names resolve to a single physical file, so the two entries cannot be represented safely. Round-tripping them through a stash would delete the file, so the Git Client refuses those operations until you resolve the collision.

remedy.title: Solution
remedy.p: Keep only one of the two colliding names. Because both names map to the same file here, the Git Client cannot stage or discard them for you — use command-line Git to remove the duplicate entry.

step.cmd: Decide which of the two names to keep.
From a command line in the repository, remove the other name from Git without deleting the file on disk.

stepresult.p: Only one entry remains, so the warning clears and the held operations become available again.

remedy.p: Alternatively, open the repository on a case-sensitive file system, where the two files are distinct, and rename or delete one of them there.
